sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: create_specifier_set
tools.description:
Create a SpecifierSet object to represent a set of version specifiers.
    
    A SpecifierSet can handle a single specifier like '>=3.0', a comma-separated list like '>=3.0,!=3.1',
    or no specifier at all. The prereleases parameter controls whether prerelease versions are accepted.
    
    Args:
        specifiers: A string representation of a specifier or comma-separated list of specifiers
        prereleases: Whether to accept prerelease versions if applicable
    
    Returns:
        String representation of the SpecifierSet object
    
    Example:
        >>> create_specifier_set('>=3.0,!=3.1')
        '>=3.0,!=3.1'

tools.name: create_version
tools.description: Create a Version object to represent a project version. version: The string representation of a version which will be parsed and normalized before use. e.g. '1.0a5' -> '<Version('1.0a5')>'.

tools.name: create_specifier
tools.description: Create a Specifier object to represent a single version specifier. spec: A version specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0.0' -> Specifier object serialized as string. prereleases: Whether to allow pre-releases.

tools.name: specifier_set_contains
tools.description:
Check if a version is contained in a SpecifierSet.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set (str): A string representation of the specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1')
        version (str): The version string to check for containment in the specifier set
        prereleases (bool | None, optional): Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet
        installed (bool | None, optional): Whether or not the item is installed
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the version is contained in the specifier set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> specifier_set_contains('>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1', '1.2.3')
        True

tools.name: is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
tools.description:
Check whether this specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    Returns True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the specifiers can never be satisfied
        
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: is_specifier_set_subset
tools.description:
Check if one SpecifierSet is a subset of another.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set (str): A string representation of the first SpecifierSet
        other_specifier_set (str): A string representation of the second SpecifierSet to check against
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the first set is a subset of the second, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_subset(">=3.12,<3.13", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: is_specifier_set_superset
tools.description:
Check if one SpecifierSet is a superset of another.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set (str): A string representation of the first SpecifierSet
        other_specifier_set (str): A string representation of the second SpecifierSet to check against
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if specifier_set is a superset of other_specifier_set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_superset(">=3.12", ">=3.12,<3.13")
        True

tools.name: is_specifier_set_disjoint
tools.description:
Check if two SpecifierSets share no matching versions.
    
    Args:
        specifier1 (str): First specifier string to form a SpecifierSet
        specifier2 (str): Second specifier string to form a SpecifierSet
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the sets share no matching versions, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_disjoint("<3.12", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: is_version_prerelease
tools.description: Check if a version is a pre-release. version: A version string to check if it is a pre-release -> true if pre-release, false otherwise.

tools.name: get_version_release
tools.description:
Get the release components of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the release components from
    
    >>> get_version_release("1.2.3")
    [1, 2, 3]
    >>> get_version_release("2.0.0")
    [2, 0, 0]
    >>> get_version_release("1!2.0.0.post0")
    [2, 0, 0]

tools.name: get_version_pre
tools.description: Get the pre-release segment of a version. version: A version string to parse -> The pre-release segment as (letter, number) tuple or None.

tools.name: get_version_post
tools.description:
Get the post-release number of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the post-release number from
    
    >>> print(get_version_post("1.2.3"))
    None
    >>> get_version_post("1.2.3.post1")
    1

tools.name: get_version_dev
tools.description: Get the development number of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the development number from -> The development number, or None if not a development version.

tools.name: get_version_local
tools.description: Get the local version segment of a version. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> 'abc'.

tools.name: is_version_postrelease
tools.description:
Check if a version is a post-release. version: A version string to check if it is a post-release -> true if post-release, false otherwise.
    
    >>> is_version_postrelease("1.2.3")
    False
    >>> is_version_postrelease("1.2.3.post1")
    True

tools.name: is_version_devrelease
tools.description: Check if a version is a development release. version: A version string to check if it is a development release -> true if development release, false otherwise.

tools.name: get_version_major
tools.description: Get the major version component. version: A version string to parse and extract the major version from, e.g. '1.2.3' -> 1.

tools.name: get_version_minor
tools.description:
Get the minor version component. version: A version string to parse and extract the minor version from
    
    >>> get_version_minor("1.2.3")
    2
    >>> get_version_minor("1")
    0

tools.name: get_version_micro
tools.description: Get the micro version component. version: A version string to parse and extract the micro version from e.g. '1.2.3' -> 3.

tools.name: get_version_epoch
tools.description:
Get the epoch of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the epoch from -> The epoch of the version.
    
    >>> get_version_epoch("2.0.0")
    0
    >>> get_version_epoch("1!2.0.0")
    1

tools.name: get_version_public
tools.description: Get the public portion of a version. version: A version string to extract the public portion from -> The public portion without local version identifiers.

tools.name: get_version_base
tools.description: Get the base version of a version. version: A version string to extract the base version from -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: canonicalize_version
tools.description: Return a canonical form of a version as a string. version: A version string to canonicalize, e.g. '1.0.0' -> '1'. strip_trailing_zero: Whether to strip trailing zeros from the release segment, e.g. '1.0.0' with strip_trailing_zero=False -> '1.0.0'.

tools.name: is_normalized_name
tools.description: Check if a name is a normalized project name. name: The name to check if it is normalized -> true if the name is normalized, false otherwise.

tools.name: parse_version
tools.description:
Parse the given version string.
    
    This is identical to the :class:`Version` constructor.
    
    >>> parse_version('1.0.dev1')
    '1.0.dev1'
    
    :param version: The version string to parse.
    :raises ValueError: When the version string is not a valid version.

tools.name: normalize_pre
tools.description: Normalize the pre-release segment of a version string. letter: The pre-release identifier to normalize, e.g. 'ALPHA' -> 'a'.

tools.name: specifier_contains
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a Specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=1.2.3'. version: The version string to check against the specifier. prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this Specifier. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440. >>> specifier_contains('>=1.2.3', '1.2.3') True

tools.name: filter_specifier
tools.description:
Filter items in the given iterable, that match the specifier.
    
    :param specifier: A version specifier string
    :param iterable: An iterable of version strings and/or Version instances
    :param prereleases: Whether or not to allow prereleases in the returned iterator
    
    >>> list(Specifier(">=1.2.3").filter(["1.2", "1.3", "1.5a1"]))
    ['1.3']

tools.name: get_specifier_operator
tools.description: Get the operator of a Specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g. '==1.2.3' -> '=='

tools.name: get_specifier_version
tools.description:
Get the version of a Specifier. specifier: A version specifier string (e.g., '==1.2.3', '>=2.0') -> The version part of the specifier.
    
    >>> get_specifier_version("==1.2.3")
    '1.2.3'

tools.name: get_full_version_range
tools.description: Return the full range of all PEP 440 versions. admit_arbitrary: whether to admit arbitrary strings as versions; prereleases: whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: get_empty_version_range
tools.description: Return the empty range with no versions. prereleases: Whether prereleases should be considered in the version range -> the empty range object

tools.name: get_singleton_version_range
tools.description: Return a strict singleton range for a specific version. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> '[1.0, 1.0]'. prereleases: Whether to include pre-releases in the range.

tools.name: range_contains
tools.description: Check if a version is contained in a VersionRange. version_range: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet. version: A version string to check against the range. prereleases: Whether to match pre-releases. None (default) uses the range's own policy. installed: When True, accept a pre-release item even if the range would not otherwise allow it. Example: range_contains(">=1.0,<2.0", "1.5") -> True.

tools.name: is_version_range_subset
tools.description:
Check if one VersionRange is a subset of another. self_range: A version range specifier string for the range to check if it's a subset, other_range: A version range specifier string for the range to check against.
    
    >>> is_version_range_subset(">=1.5,<1.8", ">=1.0,<2.0")
    True

tools.name: is_version_range_superset
tools.description: Check if one VersionRange is a superset of another. self_range: a version range specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> true if other_range is within this range.

tools.name: is_version_range_disjoint
tools.description: Check if two version ranges share no members. version_range1: A version range specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'. version_range2: Another version range specifier string, e.g. '>=2.0,<3.0'. Returns True if the ranges are disjoint, False otherwise. >>> is_version_range_disjoint('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=2.0,<3.0') True

tools.name: union_version_ranges
tools.description:
Get the union of two VersionRanges. version_range_a: First version range in PEP 440 format, version_range_b: Second version range in PEP 440 format.
    
    >>> union_version_ranges(">=1.0", "<2.0")
    '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: intersection_version_ranges
tools.description: Get the intersection of two version range specifiers. range1: first version range specifier string, range2: second version range specifier string. Example: intersection_version_ranges('>=1.0', '<2.0') -> '>=1.0,<2.0'.

tools.name: difference_version_ranges
tools.description: Get the difference between two VersionRanges. version_range_a: The first version range, expressed as a specifier set string. version_range_b: The second version range to subtract from the first, expressed as a specifier set string. Example: difference_version_ranges('>=1.0', '>=2.0') -> '>=1.0,<2.0'.

tools.name: filter_version_range
tools.description:
Yield items from iterable whose version falls inside the range defined by specifier_set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set: A string representation of a specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0')
        iterable: An iterable of version strings to filter
        prereleases: Whether to include pre-releases; if None, uses PEP 440 default behavior
    
    Example:
        >>> filter_version_range(">=1.0,<2.0", ["0.9", "1.5", "2.0"])
        ['1.5']
